- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 7–14 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment values), model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% in first 5 days of forecast window.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit recent trends; use 10–15% downward bias for next 7 days to avoid overconfidence.
